text:
mike: heads up — two nodes in us-west-2 reported Xid 31 and then ECC counts spiked. we keep losing cards during long batches and triage takes too long. can we standardize a tiny per-failure bundle so on-call can attribute quickly?

anya: yes please. current full-log bundle is heavyweight and often missing the kernel tail. what fields do you want in the mini bundle?

mike: minimal and fast to collect. idea: node-surgeon snapshot that runs on drain and on OOM/Xid trigger. something like: dmesg -T --kernel -x tail=200, journalctl -k -n 300, last 300 lines of /var/log/syslog, nv-smi quick dump, /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/information, and nvml snapshot (if nvml available). also include node metadata (instance_id, region, rack, kernel version) and pci_bus_id/gpu_index.

lee: +1. add the last nvidia-smi query of processes and memory, and the contents of /var/log/nvidia-installer.log when present. also capture `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.volatile.corrected, pci.bus_id --format=csv,noheader,nounits` to get pre/post ECC counts. keep the bundle <2MB compressed.

sam: can infra-bot produce a one-line correlation key so we can search across ES/tempo? e.g. bundle_id = sha1(node||kernel_ts||gpu_bus||failure_ts) and attach to node and to alerts.

infra-bot: auto-ack: I can emit `bundle_id` if you provide the collection hook. recommended name: rbundle-<unix_ts>-<node>-<gpu_idx>.

anya: proposal for ingest envelope (minimal fields) — put into our log-collector as one JSON per bundle: ```{
  "bundle_id": "rbundle-1812349999-i-0abc123-0",
  "node": "i-0abc123",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "kernel": "5.15.0-rc",
  "gpu_index": "0",
  "pci_bus_id": "0000:65:00.0",
  "failure_type": "Xid31",
  "failure_ts": "2026-03-18T12:34:59Z",
  "dmesg_tail": "<BASE64 gzipped content>",
  "journal_tail": "<BASE64 gzipped content>",
  "nvidia_smi_quick": "GPU 0: 8192MiB used | process list..."
}```

mike: exact. and make the failure_type a small enum we can index: XID_31, XID_79, ECC_CORRECTED_SPIKE, ECC_UNCORRECTABLE, THERMAL_THROTTLE, etc. we should also include a parsed short summary field (three-line human summary) for search/alerts.

lee: for parsing heuristics: regex for Xid variants in dmesg: "(?:NVRM: Xid \(\s*\d+\)\s*GPU at PCI: (\S+):.*Xid (\d+))". also capture ECC counts lines like "EDAC MC0: \[...\] CE count: (\d+)" or "NVRM: Caching ECC errors \(\w+\): corrected=(\d+), uncorrected=(\d+)". we can run a tiny post-processor that extracts these into top-level fields before ingestion.

olivia: operational question — when we see a bundle with repeated Xid79 on same gpu_index across 24h, do we auto-drain-and-replace or escalate to hardware? what's the threshold?

mike: proposal: if the same gpu_index on same node has >=3 Xid79 or ECC_UNCORRECTABLE within 48h, mark node for immediate drain and hardware-replace. otherwise mark for scheduling low-priority maintenance and keep monitoring. open to tweaks.

sam: cost note — mini-bundles will add storage but small. we can TTL bundles to 30 days, and keep only indexed summary fields forever (counts, bundle_id, node, failure_type).

anya: implementation plan: 1) add `rbundle-collector` script to node-surgeon repo (shell + small python helper), 2) infra-bot hook to trigger on kube node drain / agent Xid watch / manual run, 3) log-collector pipeline rule to base64-decode and uncompress fields and store raw blob in s3, parsed summary into ES. I'll make a quick PR with the collector and a sample pipeline mapping.

lee: can you paste a quick collector snippet?

mike: sure — quick shell snippet (for the thread):
```
#!/bin/bash
TS=$(date -u +%s)
NODE=$(curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id || hostname)
GPU_IDX=$1
BUNDLE=rbundle-${TS}-${NODE}-${GPU_IDX}
mkdir -p /tmp/${BUNDLE}
dmesg -T | tail -n 300 > /tmp/${BUNDLE}/dmesg.txt
journalctl -k -n 300 > /tmp/${BUNDLE}/journal_k.txt
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION,CEC,ERRORS > /tmp/${BUNDLE}/nvsmi.txt || true
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/information > /tmp/${BUNDLE}/gpu_info.txt || true
gzip -c /tmp/${BUNDLE}/dmesg.txt | base64 > /tmp/${BUNDLE}/dmesg.b64
# emit JSON to stdout for log-collector
python3 - <<PY
import json,sys
print(json.dumps({
  'bundle_id': '$BUNDLE', 'node':'$NODE', 'region':'us-west-2', 'gpu_index': str($GPU_IDX), 'pci_bus_id':'$(lspci | grep VGA | awk "{print $1}" )', 'failure_ts': str($TS), 'dmesg_tail':'`cat /tmp/${BUNDLE}/dmesg.b64`'
}))
PY
```

anya: this is great. small nit: avoid calling lspci in the heredoc python expansion — do it first and put into var. also make sure to run as non-root able to read /proc/driver/nvidia.

infra-bot: checklist created: `rbundle-collection` repo pr -> code review, pipeline mapping -> staging deploy, alert rule -> add bundle_id to alert annotations.

mike: ok i'll open the PR this afternoon. thanks all — if we get this in, triage time should drop from hours to <15min on most GPU failures. :thumbsup:

sam: +1. can we also add a tiny Grafana panel that shows recent `failure_type` counts per region? helps on-call and capacity planning.

olivia: strongly support the replacement threshold. please include an ops playbook line in the PR so on-call knows the action.

mike: will do; PR will include the playbook snippet and the regex list for Xid/ECC detection.

anya: thanks — ping me for review.
